name: authors-stability-operations
description: Stability and operations principles. No text reused.

rules.title: Integration points are treated as the primary source of failure
rules.requirement: Every call to another system is wrapped with a timeout, a failure response, and a way to stop calling when the other side is unhealthy, because integration points are where cascading failures start.

source.name: Michael Nygard
source.locator: Release It! 2nd ed., Chapter 4, Stability Antipatterns: Integration Points

rules.title: Steady state is designed, so nothing grows without bound
rules.requirement: Logs, caches, tables and queues each have a mechanism that keeps them bounded over time without human intervention, such as rotation, eviction or archival.

source.name: Michael Nygard
source.locator: Release It! 2nd ed., Stability patterns: Steady State

rules.title: Four key delivery metrics are known for the service
rules.requirement: The design or its operating plan names how deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore are measured for this service.

rules.title: Toil is identified and has a reduction plan
rules.requirement: Manual, repetitive operational work the design will create is named, and either automated in the design or scheduled for automation.

source.name: Site Reliability Engineering (Google), Chapter 5, Eliminating Toil

rules.title: Capacity and failure assumptions are revisited after incidents
rules.requirement: The operating plan names a blameless review for incidents and a path for its findings to change the design.

source.name: Site Reliability Engineering (Google), Chapter 15, Postmortem Culture
